mainTopic: סנדל המסומר: why it is forbidden on יום טוב, how many nails are allowed, and which kinds of footwear fall outside the גזירה
overview: The גמרא proves that the סנדל המסומר (spiked sandal) is forbidden on יום טוב as well as on שבת. The original incident happened at a gathering on a day when work is forbidden, so a תענית ציבור is not included. Even רבי חנינא בן עקיבא, who keeps גזירות narrow, would agree, because יום טוב and שבת differ only in אוכל נפש. שמואל limits the איסור to nails that strengthen the sandal, and רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא argue whether five or seven decorative nails are allowed. Each view is traced to a תנא, and רב אשי rules that seven is permitted and eight is forbidden. Several cases fall outside the decree: a sandal sewn from inside (it counts as a מנעל), a nail bent like tongs, and a sole fully covered with nails. A ברייתא supporting רב ששת is then explained line by line, and the הלכה is ruled against the strict view of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. רבי חייא says he would have permitted many more nails. Finally, the גמרא turns to the next line of the משנה, about going out on שבת with a single sandal.

steps.title: A source: the spiked sandal may not be sent on a Festival
steps.stepSummary: A source teaches that one may send clothing as a gift on יום טוב, but not a סנדל המסומר or an unsewn shoe. This shows the spiked sandal is forbidden on יום טוב too.
steps.simpleTranslation: We send clothing on יום טוב, whether sewn or not sewn. But we do not send a spiked sandal or an unsewn shoe on יום טוב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a source about sending gifts on יום טוב. From it we learn that a סנדל המסומר is forbidden on יום טוב, not just on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב you may only send items you are allowed to use that day. Since the spiked sandal is on the 'cannot send' list, it must be forbidden to wear on יום טוב. This is surprising, because the original גזירה was made about שבת, so the גמרא must now explain why it reaches יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A sandal with nails (spikes) in it

steps.confusionAlert: This source is about sending gifts, not about wearing shoes. The point is learned indirectly: what you may not use on יום טוב, you may not send.

phrases.english: We may send garments on a Festival
phrases.notes: Sending a gift is allowed for items usable on יום טוב.

phrases.english: whether sewn or not sewn
but not a spiked sandal

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מִנְעָל שֶׁאֵינוֹ תָּפוּר בְּיוֹם טוֹב!
phrases.english: and not an unsewn shoe, on a Festival!
phrases.notes: This is the point being proven: the spiked sandal is forbidden on יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the סנדל המסומר גזירה by asking whether it extends to יום טוב.
steps.raayaObject: That the סנדל המסומר prohibition applies on יום טוב as well as שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling that one may not send a spiked sandal as a gift on יום טוב.

steps.title: Why the decree covers the Festival: there is a gathering then too
steps.stepSummary: The גזירה on שבת exists because of a gathering of people. יום טוב also has gatherings, so the same reason applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: On שבת, what is the reason? Because there is a gathering. On יום טוב there is also a gathering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why a שבת decree also applies on יום טוב. The reason behind the decree, a crowd of people, is present on יום טוב as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original incident happened when a crowd was gathered and the spiked sandals caused deaths in a panic. Since the decree is tied to the kind of situation, a gathering, and יום טוב also brings people together, the decree carries over.

keyTerms.meaning: A gathering or assembly of people

phrases.english: On Shabbat, what is the reason?
because there is a gathering
phrases.notes: This points back to the original incident, which happened at a crowded gathering.

phrases.english: On a Festival there is also a gathering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source from step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the shared reason (gathering) that extends the decree.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decree is tied only to שבת, so יום טוב should be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The decree is tied to a gathering, which also happens on יום טוב.

steps.title: Challenge: a public fast also has a gathering
steps.stepSummary: If a gathering is the reason, then on a תענית ציבור, which also has a crowd, the spiked sandal should be forbidden too.
steps.simpleTranslation: On a public fast day there is a gathering. So it should be forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the reason just given. If any crowd is enough, the decree should also apply on public fast days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason 'there is a gathering' seems too broad. Any crowded day would then be included, yet no one forbids the spiked sandal on a תענית ציבור.

phrases.english: On a public fast day there is a gathering;
should it be forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a gathering alone is what extends the decree.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a gathering is the reason, a public fast, which also has gatherings, should be included, but it is not.

steps.title: Answer: the incident was at a gathering on a day when work is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The original incident happened at a gathering on a day when work was forbidden. A fast day is a gathering on a day when work is allowed, so it is not comparable.
steps.simpleTranslation: The incident happened at a 'gathering of prohibition.' Here it is a 'gathering of permission.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא refines the reason. Only a gathering on a day when work is forbidden matches the original incident.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבת and יום טוב are both days when work is forbidden, so they match the original case. A תענית ציבור allows work, so it does not match and the decree does not extend to it.

keyTerms.meaning: A gathering on a day when work is forbidden
A gathering on a day when work is permitted

phrases.english: When the incident happened
it was at a gathering of prohibition (a day work is forbidden)
here it is a gathering of permission (a day work is allowed).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the definition of the relevant gathering.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any gathering triggers the decree, so a fast day would be included.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a gathering on a day when work is forbidden triggers it, so שבת and יום טוב are included and a fast day is not.
steps.whatToRemember: The spiked-sandal decree applies to gatherings on days when work is forbidden (שבת and יום טוב), not to fast days.

steps.title: Even the opinion that limits decrees agrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces רבי חנינא בן עקיבא, who says decrees apply only to the exact situation of the original incident. It sets up why even he would agree here.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even according to רבי חנינא בן עקיבא, who said: They forbade only in the Jordan, in a boat, exactly like the incident that happened.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. It brings an opinion that keeps decrees narrow, so the גמרא can show the extension to יום טוב still works even by his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא בן עקיבא ruled about carrying the אפר פרה אדומה across water. He said the decree applied only to the Jordan, by boat, exactly as in the original case. One might think that by his view the sandal decree should stay limited to שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Exactly like the incident that happened

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן עֲקִיבָא, דְּאָמַר:
phrases.english: And even according to Rabbi Chanina ben Akiva, who said:
They forbade only in the Jordan and in a boat
phrases.notes: About transporting the ashes of the red heifer.

phrases.english: and exactly like the incident that occurred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Anticipates an objection to extending the decree from שבת to יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא בן עקיבא limits decrees to the precise circumstances of the original incident.

steps.title: The Jordan is unique, but יום טוב and שבת are alike
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן עקיבא limited the decree to the Jordan only because the Jordan is different from other rivers. יום טוב and שבת are not different from each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies to the Jordan, which is different from other rivers. But יום טוב and שבת are like each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why even רבי חנינא בן עקיבא would extend the sandal decree. His limit only applies when the new case really differs from the original.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Jordan has special features, such as its width and depth, so other rivers are truly different cases. יום טוב and שבת are basically the same kind of day, so extending the decree is not really a new case.

phrases.english: That applies only to the Jordan
which is different from other rivers.
But a Festival and Shabbat
are like one another,

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי יַרְדֵּן דְּשָׁאנֵי מִשְּׁאָר נְהָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the concern raised by step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing a truly unique case from a comparable one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנינא בן עקיבא would keep the decree limited to שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: He limits decrees only when the new case is truly different, and יום טוב is not different from שבת.

steps.title: Proof: the only difference is food preparation
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches that the only difference between יום טוב and שבת is preparing food. This proves the two days are alike.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: The only difference between יום טוב and שבת is food preparation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its claim that יום טוב and שבת are alike. It quotes a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה says food preparation (אוכל נפש) is the only difference, wearing shoes is not a difference. So the sandal decree carries over to יום טוב even by the narrow view.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no difference between... except

steps.whatToRemember: Even by the view that limits decrees, the spiked-sandal decree applies on יום טוב, because יום טוב and שבת differ only in אוכל נפש.

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: אֵין בֵּין יוֹם טוֹב לַשַּׁבָּת
phrases.english: as we learned: The difference between a Festival and Shabbat is
only food preparation.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: אֵין בֵּין יוֹם טוֹב לַשַּׁבָּת אֶלָּא אוֹכֶל נֶפֶשׁ בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That יום טוב and שבת are alike for this decree.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: אין בין יום טוב לשבת אלא אוכל נפש בלבד.

steps.title: Only strengthening nails are forbidden, not decorative ones
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the spiked sandal is forbidden only when the nails strengthen it. Nails added for beauty are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: They taught this only about nails that strengthen. But nails for beauty are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The גמרא now defines exactly which spiked sandals the decree covers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree targets sandals whose nails are part of how the sandal is built. Decorative nails do not make it the forbidden kind of sandal, so wearing it is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical boundary of the decree: a sandal with decorative nails may be worn on שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
They taught this only when the nails are for strengthening,
but if for beauty, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְחַזֵּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from when the decree applies to which sandals it covers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nails for strengthening make the sandal forbidden; decorative nails are permitted.

steps.title: How many nails count as decoration?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how many nails can be in the sandal and still be considered for beauty.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how many nails count as 'for beauty'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a number to define שמואל's 'for beauty' category. This sets up the next step's answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A few nails look decorative, but many nails start to function as strengthening. The גמרא wants the cutoff.

phrases.english: And how many count as for beauty?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of a term in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The maximum number of nails that still counts as decorative.

steps.title: Five per sandal or seven per sandal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says five nails in each sandal. רבי חנינא says seven in each.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: five in this one and five in that one. And רבי חנינא said: seven in this one and seven in that one.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give different numbers for the decorative limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that a small number of nails is decorative. They argue only about the cutoff: up to five per sandal, or up to seven.

keyTerms.meaning: Five in this (sandal) and five in that

steps.whatToRemember: Decorative nails are permitted, up to five per sandal (רבי יוחנן) or seven per sandal (רבי חנינא).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Five in this one and five in that one.
And Rabbi Chanina said:
Seven in this one and seven in that one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: חָמֵשׁ בָּזֶה וְחָמֵשׁ בָּזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן: up to five nails per sandal; רבי חנינא: up to seven per sandal.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן explains where the nails go
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains how the nails are placed. Under his view there are two on one side, two on the other, and one on the straps. Under רבי חנינא's view there are three, three, and one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to רב שמן בר אבא: Let me explain it to you. According to me, there are two nails on this side, two on that side, and one on the straps. According to רבי חנינא, there are three on this side, three on that side, and one on the straps.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains the numbers from the last step by showing exactly where each nail is placed on the sandal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This does not change the numbers. It only shows the layout. Five is 2+2+1, and seven is 3+3+1. In both opinions, one nail goes on the straps and the rest are split evenly between the two sides of the sole.

keyTerms.meaning: I will explain it to you
according to me / in my view
from here and from there (on this side and on that side)
its straps (the upper strap part of the sandal)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to Rav Shemen bar Abba:
I will explain it to you:
According to me, two from here (one side),
and two from there (the other side),
and one on its straps.
According to Rabbi Chanina, three from here,
and three from there, and one on its straps.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא, אַסְבְּרַהּ לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the layout behind the numbers given in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five nails means 2+2+1 on the straps. Seven nails means 3+3+1 on the straps.

steps.title: A ברייתא gives seven and thirteen nails
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. רבי נתן allows seven nails for an uneven sandal, and רבי allows thirteen. Neither number is five.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: For an uneven sandal, a person may put seven nails in it. These are the words of רבי נתן. And רבי permits it even with thirteen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to test the numbers from the previous steps. It is setting up a challenge to רבי יוחנן's 'five'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has only two opinions: seven (רבי נתן) and thirteen (רבי). Nobody in it says five. So it looks like no תנא supports רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
An uneven sandal, one may make for it seven (nails),
these are the words of Rabbi Natan.
And Rebbi permits it with thirteen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the five/seven numbers against a תנאי source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling of five nails
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's opinions are seven and thirteen. There is no opinion of five, so רבי יוחנן seems to have no תנא behind him.

steps.title: רבי חנינא fits, but whom does רבי יוחנן follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sharpens the challenge. רבי חנינא matches רבי נתן, but רבי יוחנן matches no one in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רבי חנינא: he follows רבי נתן. But רבי יוחנן, whom does he follow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the problem clearly. רבי חנינא is fine, and the real question is about רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using 'בשלמא... אלא...', the גמרא accepts that seven is the same as רבי נתן's seven. It then points out that five has no source. An אמורא is expected to follow some תנא, so this is a real problem.

keyTerms.meaning: granted / it works out fine for
like whom? (which opinion does he follow?)

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Chanina,
he spoke in line with Rabbi Natan.
But Rabbi Yochanan, like whom did he speak?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, הוּא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי נָתָן. אֶלָּא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, דְּאָמַר כְּמַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the target of the מיתיבי from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The source for רבי יוחנן's five
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Seven matches רבי נתן, but five matches no one in the ברייתא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן follows רבי נהוראי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן follows רבי נהוראי, who rules that five nails are permitted and seven are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He follows רבי נהוראי, as it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי נהוראי says, five is permitted and seven is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by finding a different ברייתא with a תנא who says exactly five.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא was not the only source. רבי נהוראי gives רבי יוחנן a clear תנא for 'five'. So the argument between רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא is really a continuation of an argument between תנאים.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי נהוראי's 'seven is forbidden' is the exact opposite of רבי חנינא's view, which follows רבי נתן. Do not think the two ברייתות agree. They disagree, and each אמורא chose a different side.

phrases.english: He spoke in line with Rabbi Nehorai,
as it was taught: Rabbi Nehorai says,
five is permitted and seven is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 12-13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's five has no source in the תנאים.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן follows רבי נהוראי, who permits five and forbids seven.

steps.title: Each group follows its own teacher
steps.stepSummary: איפה tells רבה בר בר חנה that the students of רבי יוחנן may follow רבי יוחנן, while איפה's group will follow רבי חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: איפה said to רבה בר בר חנה: You, the students of רבי יוחנן, act like רבי יוחנן. We will act like רבי חנינא.
steps.whatsHappening: The discussion ends with a practical conclusion: each group of students follows its own teacher's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views have a תנא behind them, so neither is rejected. איפה does not decide between them. He allows each group to act like its own teacher: five for רבי יוחנן's students, and seven for those who follow רבי חנינא.
steps.whatToRemember: Decorative nails are permitted: five according to רבי יוחנן (following רבי נהוראי), and seven according to רבי חנינא (following רבי נתן). Since both views have a תנא, each group of students follows its own teacher.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that when two אמוראים each have solid support from a תנא, students may follow the ruling of their own teacher in practice.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אֵיפָה לְרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חַנָּה:
phrases.english: Ifa said to Rabba bar bar Chana:
You, who are students of Rabbi Yochanan,
act like Rabbi Yochanan;
we will act like Rabbi Chanina.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אֵיפָה לְרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical conclusion after both views were shown to have תנאי support.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Students of רבי יוחנן act like him (five nails). Others follow רבי חנינא (seven nails).

steps.title: רב הונא asks whether five nails are allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא asks רב אשי what the law is for a sandal with five nails.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא asked רב אשי: a sandal with five nails, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: After the long debate about how many nails are allowed, רב הונא asks for a practical ruling about five nails. This sets up רב אשי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Five is exactly the number allowed in רבי יוחנן's view (from רבי נהוראי). רב הונא wants to know if five is safe to use and whether the limit might be higher.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (raised a question before him)

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב הוּנָא מֵרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Huna asked Rav Ashi:
Five (nails), what is the law?
phrases.notes: Five is the view of רבי יוחנן and רבי נהוראי.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב הוּנָא מֵרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the theoretical debate over the number of nails to a practical question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a sandal with five nails permitted?

steps.title: Even seven nails are permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that not only five, but even seven nails are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: even seven is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question. Five is fine, and you can go all the way up to seven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By allowing seven, רב אשי follows רבי חנינא, who matches רבי נתן. This fits איפה's earlier statement that his group follows רבי חנינא, not רבי יוחנן's limit of five.

keyTerms.meaning: Even (the answer goes beyond what was asked)

steps.confusionAlert: The word אֲפִילּוּ means רב אשי is giving MORE than was asked. Five was asked about, and he says even seven is fine.

phrases.english: He said to him: Even seven is permitted.
phrases.notes: He's going with רבי חנינא and רבי נתן here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Up to seven nails is permitted, following רבי חנינא.

steps.title: רב הונא asks about nine nails
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא follows up and asks about nine nails.
steps.simpleTranslation: Nine, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא asks a follow-up question to find where the limit is. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since seven is allowed, he checks whether the number might go higher. Nine is between seven and רבי's thirteen from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Nine, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up question testing the upper limit.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a sandal with nine nails permitted?

steps.title: Even eight nails are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that not only nine, but even eight nails are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: even eight is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי sets the ceiling. Seven is the most you may have, so eight or more is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the law does not follow רבי's thirteen. The firm line is seven, so the rule follows רבי נתן's seven exactly.
steps.whatToRemember: Practical ruling: up to seven nails is permitted, and eight or more is forbidden.

phrases.english: He said to him: Even eight is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 and sets the upper limit.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Eight or more nails is forbidden. The limit is seven.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Seven nails is the maximum allowed.

steps.title: A shoemaker asks about a sandal sewn from the inside
steps.stepSummary: A shoemaker asks רבי אמי about a nailed sandal whose sole was sewn on from the inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain shoemaker asked רבי אמי: if he sewed it from the inside, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new case is raised: the sole was stitched on from the inside instead of the outside. This sets up רבי אמי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether this way of making it changes what the item is. If it is no longer a 'sandal,' the decree on nailed sandals may not apply.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ הָהוּא רַצְעָנָא מֵרַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: A certain shoemaker asked Rabbi Ami:
If he sewed it from the inside, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ הָהוּא רַצְעָנָא מֵרַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New case about how the sandal is built, not how many nails it has.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the decree apply to a nailed sandal sewn from the inside?

steps.title: רבי אמי permits it but does not know why
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי rules it is permitted but admits he does not know the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: it is permitted, and I do not know the reason.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי gives the ruling (permitted) but honestly says he has no explanation for it. This leaves room for the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He knows the ruling as a received tradition but not its logic. In the next step, רב אשי supplies the reason.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is permitted,
and I do not know the reason.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מוּתָּר, וְלָא יָדַעְנָא מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the shoemaker's question.

steps.title: רב אשי explains: sewn from inside makes it a shoe
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives the reason: sewn from inside, it counts as a shoe (מנעל), and the decree was only on sandals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Does the master really not know the reason? Since he sewed it from the inside, it is a shoe. The רבנן made their decree about a sandal, but not about a shoe.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי fills in the missing reason for רבי אמי's ruling. He is surprised it was not obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sewing from inside changes the item's identity from סנדל to מנעל. The decree against nailed footwear was made only for sandals, so a shoe with nails stays permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: The decree was on a nailed סנדל only. A nailed מנעל, including a sandal sewn from inside, is permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the decree is defined by the type of footwear: it was made on a סנדל. Once the item counts as a מנעל, it falls outside the decree, even though it has nails.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
And does the master not know the reason?!
Since he sewed it from the inside,
it is a shoe.
Regarding a sandal, the Rabbis decreed;
regarding a shoe, the Rabbis did not decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: וְלָא יָדַע מָר מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the reason missing from step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassification: the item belongs to a category the decree never covered.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A nailed sandal sewn from inside is still a sandal and should be forbidden, so the permission seems unexplained.
steps.terutzMaskana: It counts as a מנעל, and the decree was only on a סנדל.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Nailed shoes are not included in the decree.

steps.title: Question about a nail bent like tongs
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר זבדא asks רבי אבא בר אבינא about a nail bent into the shape of tongs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר זבדא asked רבי אבא בר אבינא: if he shaped it like tongs, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new case is asked: a nail bent so both ends go into the sandal, like tongs. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shape of the nail is different from a normal nail. The question is whether this kind of nail falls under the decree.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a kind of tongs (a bent nail with both ends inserted)

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Zavda asked
Rabbi Abba bar Avina:
If he shaped it like tongs, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא מֵרַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר אֲבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another case testing the limits of the decree.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a sandal with a tongs-shaped nail permitted?

steps.title: A tongs-shaped nail is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר אבינא rules it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is short. A nail shaped like tongs does not make the sandal forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not give a reason here. The point is that this shape falls outside the decree.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23.

steps.title: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says the same
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the ruling with a matching statement from רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: if he shaped it like tongs, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the previous answer. Another אמורא said the same ruling independently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי introduce a second source that agrees. This strengthens the ruling that a tongs-shaped nail is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (introduces a supporting statement)

steps.whatToRemember: The decree on nailed sandals has limits. Up to seven nails is allowed, a sandal sewn from inside counts as a shoe, and a tongs-shaped nail is permitted.

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
If he shaped it like tongs, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 24 with an independent statement.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that a tongs-shaped nail is permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.

steps.title: A sole fully covered with nails is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת rules that if the entire sole is covered with nails to protect it from the ground, the sandal may be worn on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: If he covered the whole sole with nails so that the ground will not wear it away, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת adds a new case about nailed sandals. If the nails cover the entire sole only to protect it from wear, wearing it is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree was made against the typical סנדל המסומר, a sandal with scattered spikes or studs. A sole completely covered in nails looks and works like armor plating for the sole, so it does not match the type of sandal that was banned. The sandal is still nailed, but it falls outside the decree.

keyTerms.meaning: A nailed sandal, which the Rabbis prohibited wearing on שבת

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
If he covered it entirely with nails
so that the ground will not wear it away,
phrases.notes: The purpose is protection, not spikes.

phrases.english: it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of nailed-sandal cases that are permitted, after the bent nail shaped like tongs in steps 23-25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sole fully covered in nails for protection is permitted on שבת.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב ששת and lists the nailed-sandal laws
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lays out the rules of סנדל המסומר. It ends with the same case as רב ששת: a sole fully covered with nails is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in agreement with רב ששת: A man may not go out in a nailed sandal, nor walk in it from house to house, or even from bed to bed. But one may move it to cover a vessel or to prop up bed legs, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון forbids even that. If most of its nails fell out and four or five remain, it is permitted, and רבי permits up to seven. If he covered it with leather from below and put nails in from above, it is permitted. If he made the nail like tongs, like a flat plate, or like a peg, or covered the whole sole with nails so the ground won't wear it away, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches רב ששת's ruling. Along the way, the ברייתא lists the main rules of the nailed sandal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree only bans wearing the sandal, even indoors. It does not ban moving it for some other use, though רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון is stricter. The ברייתא then lists cases that fall outside the decree: few nails left, nails hidden under leather, nails with a changed shape, or a fully nailed sole. The last case is exactly רב ששת's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught (in a ברייתא) in agreement with him
We may move or carry it
A tongs-shaped bend in the nail

steps.confusionAlert: 'From bed to bed' is about wearing the sandal, even indoors. Moving it by hand for another use is a separate matter, and the ברייתא allows that.

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav Sheshet:
A man may not go out in a nailed sandal,
and he may not walk in it from house to house,
even from bed to bed.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מְטַלְטְלִין אוֹתוֹ לְכַסּוֹת בּוֹ אֶת הַכְּלִי
phrases.english: But one may move it to cover a vessel with it
and to prop up the legs of the bed with it.
And Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon forbids it.
If most of its nails fell out

phrases.aramaic: וְנִשְׁתַּיְּירוּ בּוֹ אַרְבַּע אוֹ חָמֵשׁ — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: and four or five remained in it, it is permitted.
And Rabbi permits up to seven.
If he covered it with leather from below
and fixed nails in it from above, it is permitted.
If he made it like a kind of tongs

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ כְּמִין טַס אוֹ כְּמִין יָתֵד,
phrases.english: or like a kind of plate, or like a kind of peg,
or if he covered it entirely with nails

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא קַרְקַע אוֹכַלְתּוֹ — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: so that the ground will not wear it away, it is permitted.
phrases.notes: This is the line that supports רב ששת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that supports רב ששת's ruling in step 26.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's ruling that a sole fully covered with nails is permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (תוספתא) that ends with the identical case: חיפהו כולו במסמרות … מותר.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to contradict itself on leftover nails
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes a contradiction inside the ברייתא. 'Most nails fell out' allows many to remain, yet the next words limit it to four or five.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא itself is difficult. You said 'most of its nails fell out', which implies it is permitted even if many still remain. Then it teaches 'four or five': that many, yes; more, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא it just quoted. Two parts of the same line seem to give different rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose a sandal had many nails. 'Most fell out' alone suggests that even a large number left over is fine, as long as most are gone. But the ברייתא also says 'four or five remained', which suggests anything above five is forbidden. These two measures can clash.

keyTerms.meaning: This source itself is difficult (it contradicts itself)

phrases.english: This itself is difficult.
You said: 'most of its nails fell out',

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּנִשְׁתַּיְּירוּ בֵּיהּ טוּבָא,
phrases.english: even though many remained in it,
and then it teaches:
four or five, yes;
more, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from using the ברייתא as proof to questioning how its own internal wording fits together.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's line 'נשרו רוב מסמרותיו ונשתיירו בו ארבע או חמש'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Most fell out' implies there is no upper limit on what remains, while 'four or five' sets a fixed limit. The two measures contradict each other.

steps.title: Broken-off nails versus fully removed nails
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the 'most fell out' rule covers nails that broke off and left visible stumps. The 'four or five' rule covers nails pulled out completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: It is not difficult. Here, the nails were broken off. There, the nails were uprooted completely.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת resolves the contradiction by assigning each measure to a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When nails break off, their stumps stay in the sole. Anyone can see that most are gone, so the 'most' rule applies even if many whole nails remain. When nails are pulled out completely, no trace is left. All anyone sees is the nails still there, so only four or five are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces a resolution)
Here … there (assigning each statement to a different case)

steps.whatToRemember: Two measures apply to a nailed sandal. If most nails broke off and the stumps show, it is permitted even with many left. If the nails were fully removed, only four or five may remain, and רבי allows up to seven. A fully nailed sole made for protection is permitted entirely.
steps.whyThisMatters: The decree depends on how the sandal looks. What matters is what an observer can see, not only how many nails are physically present.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: It is not difficult:
here, where they were broken off,
phrases.notes: Stumps remain, so it is visible that most are gone.

phrases.english: there, where they were uprooted.
phrases.notes: No trace remains, so only the leftover nails are seen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the internal contradiction raised in step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (כאן … כאן): each measure applies to a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both measures seemed to apply to the same case of nails falling out, which made them contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Most fell out' applies to broken-off nails whose stumps show. 'Four or five' applies to nails that were fully removed.

steps.title: Why mention four if five is already allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's words 'four or five is permitted' and asks why four needs mentioning if five is already allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said 'four or five is permitted.' Now, if five is allowed, do we even need to be told that four is allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's phrase 'four or five' and attacks its wording. If more nails (five) are allowed, fewer nails (four) should obviously be allowed too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With nails, more is stricter, because more nails make the sandal more like the forbidden סנדל המסומר. So if five is allowed, four must be allowed as well. Mentioning four seems pointless, and the גמרא wants to know what the ברייתא means.

keyTerms.meaning: Now: introduces the logic 'if this is true, then surely...'
Is it necessary [to say]? Asks why an obvious case was mentioned

phrases.english: Four or five is permitted.
phrases.notes: Quoting the ברייתא from the previous steps.

phrases.english: Now, if five is permitted,
is it necessary to say four?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues analyzing the ברייתא's wording right after רב ששת's answer in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's phrase 'four or five is permitted.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the larger number is permitted, the smaller number is obviously permitted, so stating four is redundant.

steps.title: Four for a small sandal, five for a large one
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that 'four' refers to a small sandal and 'five' refers to a large sandal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: four nails for a small sandal, and five nails for a large sandal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. The two numbers are not one rule; they are two limits for two different sandal sizes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not saying 'four, and certainly five.' It is giving each size its own limit. A small sandal may keep only four nails, while a large sandal may keep five. So four is not redundant: for a small sandal, five would be too many.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'four or five' as 'either number, it doesn't matter.' Each number belongs to a different size of sandal.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Four, from a small sandal,
and five, from a large sandal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: אַרְבַּע מִסַּנְדָּל קָטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each number applies to a different sandal size.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Four and five are one rule, so four is redundant.
steps.terutzMaskana: Four is the limit for a small sandal and five is the limit for a large one.

steps.title: Does רבי allow seven nails or thirteen?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says רבי permits up to seven nails. Another ברייתא says רבי permits up to thirteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says: and רבי permits up to seven. But wasn't it taught in another ברייתא: רבי permits up to thirteen!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא, that רבי allows up to seven nails. It then points out that a different ברייתא quotes רבי as allowing thirteen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same תנא, רבי, seems to give two different numbers. Seven and thirteen cannot both be his limit for the same sandal, so the גמרא needs to explain the difference.

phrases.english: And Rabbi permits up to seven.
phrases.notes: Quoting the next line of the ברייתא.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: רַבִּי מַתִּיר עַד שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה!
phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: Rabbi permits up to thirteen!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: רַבִּי מַתִּיר עַד שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the same ברייתא and finds a conflict with another ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's limit of seven nails in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא quotes רבי as allowing thirteen, which contradicts a limit of seven.

steps.title: An uneven sole is different
steps.stepSummary: The thirteen-nail ruling is about a sandal whose sole is uneven (נוטה), which is a different case.
steps.simpleTranslation: A sandal with an uneven sole is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers in two words. The thirteen-nail ruling deals with a sandal whose sole is uneven or slanted (נוטה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a נוטה sandal, the nails are put in to level out the sole, not to make it a spiked sandal. So it does not look like the forbidden סנדל המסומר, and more nails are allowed. The limit of seven covers a normal, even sandal.

keyTerms.meaning: Tilted or uneven: a sandal whose sole slants

phrases.english: An uneven [sandal] is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: a normal sandal versus an uneven (נוטה) sandal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי gave two conflicting limits for the same sandal.
steps.terutzMaskana: Seven is for a normal sandal; thirteen is for a נוטה sandal, whose nails serve to level it.

steps.title: The same answer helps רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: Now that we know a נוטה sandal is different, the earlier difficulty against רבי יוחנן is also solved.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this idea, for רבי יוחנן it is also not difficult: an uneven sandal is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to an earlier difficulty against רבי יוחנן's lower nail count. It says the new idea, that a נוטה sandal is different, solves that problem too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן gave a smaller number of nails than the תנאים in the ברייתא, which looked like he was going against them. Now we can say their higher numbers were only for a נוטה sandal. For a regular sandal, even they would agree with רבי יוחנן's lower limit.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have arrived at this: using a new answer to solve an older problem

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of נוטה does double duty. It settles the contradiction about רבי and also removes the conflict between רבי יוחנן and the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Now that you have arrived at this,
for Rabbi Yochanan it is also not difficult:
an uneven [sandal] is different.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דַּאֲתֵית לְהָכִי, לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the answer of step 33 and applies it to an earlier difficulty against רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reusing a new distinction to resolve an older difficulty.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's lower limit conflicts with the higher numbers in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא's higher numbers are about a נוטה sandal, so רבי יוחנן's limit for a normal sandal stands.

steps.title: The הלכה does not follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה (or, some say, רב אחדבוי בר מתנה quoting him) rules that the הלכה is not like רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said (and some say רב אחדבוי בר מתנה said in the name of רב מתנה): the הלכה is not like רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: A practical ruling is given. We do not follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who was strict about the nailed sandal in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון was the strictest opinion; he forbade even moving a סנדל המסומר. רב מתנה rules against him, so the more lenient view of the other תנאים is the הלכה. The גמרא records two versions of who said it, but the ruling is the same.

phrases.english: Rav Mattana said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב אַחָדְבוּי בַּר מַתְנָה
phrases.english: and some say Rav Achadvoi bar Mattana said
that Rav Mattana said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.english: The halacha is not like Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the ברייתא to ruling on which opinion is the halacha.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The halacha does not follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's strict view on the nailed sandal.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious? One against many
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ruling was needed, since the הלכה always follows the majority over a lone opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! When it is one person against many, the הלכה follows the many!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב מתנה's ruling as unnecessary. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון stood alone against the others, and we always follow the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule: יחיד ורבים הלכה כרבים. Since רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון was a single voice against the many, we already know not to follow him. So why did רב מתנה have to say it?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious: challenges a statement as unnecessary
One against many: the הלכה follows the many

phrases.english: That is obvious,
[between] an individual and many, the halacha is like the many!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רב מתנה's ruling in step 35 was needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מתנה's ruling against רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The general majority rule already gives this result, so the ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: His reasoning seemed strong, so it needed saying
steps.stepSummary: The ruling was needed because one might have thought רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's reasoning was especially convincing here.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: the reasoning of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון makes good sense in this case. So רב מתנה teaches us that it is not the הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב מתנה had to rule. Without his statement, someone might follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון because his reasoning sounds so good here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes a strong logical reason could make us think a lone opinion should win. רב מתנה tells us that even so, the majority rule stands. This is the classic מהו דתימא / קא משמע לן structure: it names the mistake we might have made and then corrects it.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said: introduces the mistaken assumption
It teaches us: the new point being made

steps.whatToRemember: With סנדל המסומר: four nails may stay on a small sandal and five on a large one. A נוטה (uneven) sandal is different and may have more. The הלכה does not follow the strict view of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, even though his reasoning seemed strong.

phrases.english: You might have said:

phrases.aramaic: מִסְתַּבְּרָא טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּהָא,
phrases.english: the reasoning of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon is convincing in this case,
so it teaches us [that it is not the halacha].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'it's obvious' challenge of step 36.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: explains the mistake the ruling prevents.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because his reasoning seemed especially strong here, we might follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון despite being outnumbered.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even so, the הלכה does not follow him; the majority rule stands.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ruling against רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון is needed to stop us from following his convincing-sounding but minority opinion.

steps.title: רבי חייא would have permitted many nails
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא says he would have permitted many nails in a sandal, but he held back because people would call him a Babylonian who permits forbidden things.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא said: If people would not call me 'the Babylonian who permits forbidden things,' I would permit a lot of nails in it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא gives his own, more lenient view on how many nails a סנדל המסומר may have. He explains that he does not rule this way in public because of how people would react.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps gave small numbers of nails that are allowed. רבי חייא held that the true law allows many more. רבי חייא came from בבל to ארץ ישראל, and he worried that a lenient ruling would get him labeled as a foreigner who is careless with איסורים, so he held back.

keyTerms.meaning: A sandal with nails in its sole, which the חכמים forbade wearing on שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a חכם holding back from ruling leniently so that his reputation, and the public's respect for the law, would not be harmed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya said:
If not for the fact that they would call me
'Babylonian who permits prohibitions'
phrases.notes: This is a mocking label people would give him.

phrases.english: I would permit many nails in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא: אִי לָאו דְּקָרוּ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the question of how many nails are allowed, and adds a more lenient opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In principle רבי חייא would allow many nails, but he does not say so publicly because of how people would see it.

steps.title: How many nails did he mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what number of nails רבי חייא would have permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how many?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact number behind רבי חייא's word 'many.' This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא only said 'a lot.' The גמרא wants a specific number so the opinion can be clearly defined.

phrases.english: And how many?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact meaning of רבי חייא's word 'many.'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact number of nails רבי חייא would have permitted.

steps.title: פומבדיתא says twenty-four, סורא says twenty-two
steps.stepSummary: Two יישיבות report different numbers: פומבדיתא says twenty-four nails, and סורא says twenty-two.
steps.simpleTranslation: In פומבדיתא they say twenty-four. In סורא they say twenty-two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with two traditions. Each comes from a different Babylonian יישיבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both traditions agree that רבי חייא meant a large number. They differ only on whether the number was twenty-four or twenty-two.

keyTerms.meaning: פומבדיתא, a major Torah center in בבל
סורא, another major Torah center in בבל

phrases.english: In Pumbedita they said: Twenty-four.
In Sura they said: Twenty-two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'how many' question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Twenty-four nails according to פומבדיתא, and twenty-two according to סורא.

steps.title: A memory trick: two nails lost on the road
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a memory trick. By the time רבי חייא traveled from פומבדיתא to סורא, his sandal had lost two nails.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Here is your sign to remember. By the time he came from פומבדיתא to סורא, he was missing two nails.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a סימן, a memory aid, so you remember which city said which number. It does not add a new law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture רבי חייא leaving פומבדיתא with twenty-four nails in his sandal. On the road to סורא, two nails fall out, so he arrives with twenty-two. That way you know the higher number belongs to פומבדיתא and the lower number belongs to סורא.
steps.confusionAlert: This is only a memory trick. It does not mean the law really changed on the trip or that רבי חייא actually lost nails.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי חייא would have allowed many nails, either 24 (פומבדיתא) or 22 (סורא). The trick: you lose two nails on the road from פומבדיתא to סורא.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said,
And your mnemonic is:
By the time he came from Pumbedita to Sura
he lost two.
phrases.notes: Two nails fell off his sandal along the way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, וְסִימָנָיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a way to remember the two numbers from the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Memory aid: twenty-four goes with פומבדיתא and twenty-two goes with סורא.

steps.title: New משנה line: going out with one sandal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה. One may not go out wearing a single sandal unless there is a wound on his foot.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not with a single sandal, when there is no wound on his foot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line of the משנה and quotes it as a heading. It is setting up a new discussion that will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic shifts from nailed sandals to wearing only one sandal on שבת. The משנה forbids this when the foot is healthy, which suggests the case is different when there is a wound. The גמרא will now explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: With a single one, meaning one sandal

phrases.english: And not with a single sandal
when there is no wound on his foot.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא בְּיָחִיד בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בְּרַגְלוֹ מַכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the nailed-sandal discussion and quotes the next clause of the משנה to begin a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not go out on שבת wearing a single sandal unless there is a wound on his foot.
